c.tagline: A glamorous Tyrrhenian island of cliffside villas, the luminous Blue Grotto, and iconic sea-stack Faraglioni

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small boutiques and boat operators

taxi.fare: Metered, but often high fixed rates in peak season
taxi.fareNote: Capri's small, winding roads mean taxis are open-top convertibles; fares are notably higher than mainland Italy

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Capri Town and Anacapri are each walkable, but hilly with many stairs; getting between the two towns is by funicular, bus, or taxi

safety.safety: Very safe island, extremely crowded with day-trippers in peak season
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded areas during peak season is the main concern

hood_landmark.Capri Town (Piazzetta): The Piazzetta (Piazza Umberto I), Capri's famous small square
hood_landmark.Marina Grande: Marina Grande, the island's main harbor
hood_landmark.Anacapri: Villa San Michele and the Monte Solaro chairlift
hood_landmark.Marina Piccola: Marina Piccola's swimming cove beneath the Faraglioni

avoid.reason: Nothing dangerous — just overpriced taxis, restaurants and boat tours; confirm prices before committing.

hood_desc: The elegant hilltop town centered on its famous small square, packed with designer boutiques, cafes, and the best people-watching on the island.
The main harbor where ferries and boats arrive, connected to Capri Town by funicular; less glamorous but the practical entry point.
The quieter, higher western town, with Villa San Michele and access to Monte Solaro's panoramic chairlift.
A small pebble cove below the Gardens of Augustus, popular for swimming with views of the Faraglioni sea stacks.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink, though many order bottled at restaurants.

transit.sys: Funicular between Marina Grande and Capri Town, plus local bus routes to Anacapri and Marina Piccola
transit.pay: Single tickets or a combined day pass, sold at kiosks
transit.note: Private cars are largely restricted on the island; the funicular, buses, and taxis handle most transport

transport.air: Naples International Airport (NAP), then a ferry from Naples or Sorrento
transport.train: Circumvesuviana train to Sorrento connects with the ferry to Capri
transport.bus: Local buses connect Capri Town, Anacapri, and Marina Piccola
transport.ferry: Frequent ferries and hydrofoils from Naples, Sorrento, and Positano
transport.car: Not practical for visitors; the island is largely car-free for tourists

airport.name: Naples International Airport (via ferry)
airport.distance: ~40 km to Naples port, then a 45-80 min ferry crossing
airport.transport: Taxi/train to Naples or Sorrento port, then ferry to Capri

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for boat and tour guides
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture

food.name: Ravioli Capresi
food.desc: Small round ravioli filled with caciotta cheese and marjoram, dressed in nothing more than fresh tomato and basil; the island's defining plate.

places.name: Lo Sfizio
places.note: No view, no frills, priced for locals; its ravioli capresi is repeatedly named the island's best.

places.name: Da Gelsomina alla Migliara
places.note: Family farm restaurant up the Migliara path making ravioli and rabbit from its own land.

places.name: La Savardina
places.area: Via Lo Capo, near Villa Jovis
places.note: Citrus-grove garden away from the crowds, cooking classic Caprese home dishes.

food.name: Insalata Caprese
food.desc: Buffalo mozzarella, ripe tomato and basil layered with olive oil and nothing else. Invented here, and still eaten as a light lunch rather than a starter.

places.name: Da Paolino
places.note: Tables under a canopy of lemon trees; the island's most photographed dining room.

places.name: Ristorante Aurora
places.note: Family-run since the 1920s, famous for pizza all'acqua and impeccable simple plates.

places.name: Le Grottelle
places.note: Cave-backed terrace on the cliff walk, doing straightforward Caprese cooking with a view.

food.name: Totani e Patate
food.desc: Local flying squid stewed slowly with potatoes, tomato and chilli until both go soft and sweet; the island's true home-kitchen classic.

places.name: Da Gemma
places.note: Old-town trattoria in a stone-vaulted room, strong on traditional island seafood.

places.name: Lo Sfizio
places.note: Everyday Caprese cooking at prices islanders actually pay.

places.name: Ristorante Il Riccio
places.note: Michelin-starred seaside kitchen that treats local squid and shellfish with real precision.

food.name: Pezzogna all'Acqua Pazza
food.desc: Blue-spotted sea bream from the Gulf of Naples poached in crazy water of tomato, garlic, parsley and sea water; the local fish, cooked the local way.

places.name: Ristorante Il Riccio
places.note: Cliffside seafood restaurant known for whole local fish and a famous dessert room.

places.name: Le Grottelle
places.note: Whole fish and seafood pasta served on a terrace over the sea.

places.name: Da Paolino
places.note: Buffet-heavy but does whole local fish well under the lemon trees.

food.name: Torta Caprese
food.desc: Flourless almond and dark chocolate cake with a cracked top and fudgy centre, said to be the result of a baker forgetting the flour.

places.name: Pasticceria Buonocore
places.note: Island institution for torta caprese and waffle-cone gelato; the smell fills the street.

places.name: Da Gemma
places.note: Serves a proper homemade torta caprese to finish a traditional meal.

places.name: Bar Tiberio
places.note: Piazzetta cafe where a slice with an espresso is the classic afternoon stop.

food.name: Melanzane al Cioccolato
food.desc: A Sorrentine-peninsula oddity eaten around Ferragosto: fried aubergine slices layered with dark chocolate, candied peel and almonds, served cold.

places.name: Da Gelsomina alla Migliara
places.note: Traditional Anacapri kitchen that still makes the old feast-day sweets in season.

places.name: La Savardina
places.area: Via Lo Capo, near Villa Jovis
places.note: Family restaurant with homemade desserts that change with the calendar.

places.name: Pasticceria Buonocore
places.note: Stocks the island's traditional sweets alongside its famous cake and gelato.

food.name: Limoncello
food.desc: Iced lemon liqueur made from the thick fragrant peel of local sfusato lemons, poured after dinner and drunk in one cold, sweet mouthful.

places.name: Limoncello di Capri
places.note: The producer that trademarked the name in 1988, with shops offering free tastings.

places.name: Da Paolino
places.note: Dinner ends with limoncello poured under the restaurant's own lemon trees.

places.name: Bar Tiberio
places.note: Good place for a limoncello while watching the Piazzetta parade go past.

food.name: Campanian White Wine
food.desc: Crisp volcanic whites from the mainland such as Falanghina, Greco di Tufo and Fiano, the standard pour with Capri's seafood and cheese dishes.

places.name: Ristorante Il Riccio
places.note: Deep Campanian cellar built to match its seafood tasting menus.

places.name: Terrazza Tiberio
places.note: Panoramic hotel terrace with a strong regional list and contemporary Italian cooking.

places.name: Ristorante Aurora
places.note: Long-established family restaurant with a well-kept list of southern Italian wines.

landmarks: Grotta Azzurra (Blue Grotto)
Rowboats slip through a meter-high opening into this sea cave where sunlight refracts into an otherworldly electric-blue glow that has mesmerized visitors since Roman emperors.
Faraglioni Rocks
Three colossal limestone stacks rising from sapphire water form Capri's signature image; boats thread the natural arch of the middle rock for luck and kisses.
Piazzetta (Piazza Umberto I)
The tiny, theatrical 'world's living room' where cafe tables, the clock tower, and celebrity-watching converge above the port, best savored with a pricey aperitivo.
Giardini di Augusto and Via Krupp
Flower-filled terraced gardens overlooking the Faraglioni, poised above the vertiginous hairpin switchbacks of Via Krupp zigzagging down the cliff to Marina Piccola.
Monte Solaro Chairlift
A dreamy single-seat chairlift floats from Anacapri to Capri's 589-meter summit, unveiling a 360-degree panorama across the island, Vesuvius, and the Amalfi Coast.
Villa San Michele
Swedish physician Axel Munthe's white villa in Anacapri weaves gardens, ancient sculptures, and an Egyptian sphinx into one of the Mediterranean's most romantic viewpoints.
Villa Jovis
Emperor Tiberius ruled Rome from this clifftop palace for a decade; its sprawling ruins crown a 334-meter precipice with staggering views toward Sorrento.
Arco Naturale
A soaring Paleolithic limestone arch framing cobalt sea far below, reached by a scenic footpath through pine woods east of Capri town.
Marina Piccola
Capri's sheltered southern cove, where pebbly beach clubs face the Faraglioni and legend places the sirens' rock that tempted Odysseus.
Certosa di San Giacomo
A serene 14th-century Carthusian monastery amid gardens above Marina Piccola, its cloisters now host art exhibitions and dreamy Faraglioni vistas.

train.note: Capri is an island with no railway. The mainland railheads are Naples Centrale for Trenitalia (https://www.trenitalia.com) national services and Sorrento at the end of the Circumvesuviana line (https://www.eavsrl.it/); from either you continue by ferry. The island's own funicular climbs from Marina Grande up to Capri town.

bus.note: No coach routes exist on an island. Small ATC buses shuttle between Marina Grande, Capri town, Anacapri and the Blue Grotto on a road too narrow for anything larger, running every 15-20 minutes and packed in summer; the chairlift to Monte Solaro goes from Anacapri.

intl.to: Naples - Molo Beverello & Calata Porta di Massa (Italy) - 50 min hydrofoil or 80 min car ferry

ferry.note: Everything arrives at Marina Grande. Hydrofoils from Naples take under an hour and run all year; the slower Caremar car ferry is cheaper, though note that non-residents cannot bring cars to Capri for much of the year. Amalfi Coast sailings are seasonal, roughly April to October. Boats are cancelled in rough weather - in winter check the forecast before committing to a day trip.

half.name: Positano
half.blurb: Cliffside Amalfi Coast village of pastel houses stacked steeply above the sea, reached from Capri by hydrofoil.

half.name: Sorrento
half.blurb: Clifftop town overlooking the Bay of Naples, known for its limoncello production and views across to Mount Vesuvius.

half.name: Naples
half.blurb: Mainland port city with Europe's oldest continuously operating archaeological museum and a historic center dating to Greek times.
